name: 楚能新能源股份有限公司 (CORNEX NEW ENERGY CO., LTD.)
headquarters: No. 1 Cornex Avenue (楚能大道特1号), Linkong Economic Zone, Xiaogan (孝感), Hubei, China — the global headquarters inaugurated 22 November 2024; the company was founded in and runs its research, manufacturing and technology centres from Wuhan's Jiangxia district (武汉江夏), where its ICP filings are registered
employees: Not published. R&D staff 'over 2,200' (Wuhan municipal government, February 2026) and 'over 2,250, more than half with master's or doctoral degrees' (company product manual, October 2025); a job-board figure of 'over 10,000' total is unverified. Jobs promised per base: Xiangyang over 5,000, Yichang phase 2 6,000, Wuhan phase 2 about 6,000

ownership.ticker: Private (founder-controlled: 代德明 / Dai Deming via 恒信汽车集团 and 湖北恒信德龙实业 — percentages are aggregator data the company has never published; no listing, no listing filing)

summary:
**BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** Cornex (楚能新能源) is the fastest-rising storage-cell maker in this corpus — seventh on SNE Research's H1-2026 table at 30.2 GWh and 6.5% share, from outside the top ten two years earlier, and the last of the SNE top twelve to be profiled — built in five years on one car dealer's cash and Hubei's land, with two new 70–80 GWh plants commissioned in August 2026 ten months after groundbreaking. It has never published an audited financial statement, holds no listing and has filed for none anywhere, and its owner has just committed RMB 10 billion of his own money to a separate car-making venture.

**BACKGROUND.** 楚能新能源股份有限公司 / CORNEX NEW ENERGY CO., LTD., a joint-stock company founded in Wuhan in August 2021 by 代德明 (Dai Deming), the founder of 恒信汽车集团 (Hengxin Automobile Group, China's fourth-largest car-dealer group, revenue RMB 78.5 billion on the 2025 China Top 500). Control runs through 恒信汽车集团 and 湖北恒信德龙实业有限公司; the widely repeated figures — 76.15% of equity and 92.5% of votes — are aggregator data, and an August 2026 investigative piece gives a different cut (55% / 25% / 12.5% / 7.5%); the company itself publishes no shareholder table, registered capital or accounts. Four Hubei bases: Wuhan Jiangxia (production from November 2022), Xiaogan (June 2023; global headquarters), Yichang phase 1 (65 GWh, August 2023) and phase 2 (80 GWh, RMB 22 billion, commissioned 9 August 2026), and Xiangyang (70 GWh, commissioned 30 August 2026); Wuhan phase 2 (80 GWh, RMB 22 billion) was signed on 8 February 2026 for production in Q1 2027, and the chairman's target is 'over 500 GWh' of capacity by the end of 2026 against 'over 110 GWh' effective, a figure the company has repeated unchanged since December 2024. Products run from 100Ah to 588Ah prismatic LFP storage cells (648Ah and 688Ah shown), the CORNEX M5 5 MWh and M6 6.26 MWh 20-foot containers, the 浸默 (Jinmo) immersion fire-suppression system, EV traction cells including the 珠峰 (Everest) 6C fast-charge cell, truck and marine cells, and sodium-ion. Shipments: 'over 20 GWh' in 2024 per the company, 'over 90 GWh' in 2025 per InfoLink and trade press, and 30.2 GWh for H1 2026 per SNE against 'over 40 GWh' per the company. Rank depends on the house — SNE seventh, InfoLink, TrendForce and ICC sixth, Benchmark fifth (+116% year on year), SPIR third, and the 'global top three' the company and the Wuhan and Hubei governments repeat rests on SPIR. Framework signings in 2026 total over 100 GWh (CIBF 50 GWh including CRRC Zhuzhou Institute 25 GWh; some 40 GWh overseas across Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Europe, Latin America and Southeast Asia), and supply commitments have been scaled to match (Longpan Technology 1.3 million tonnes of LFP cathode to 2030, over RMB 45 billion; Tinci 1.01 million tonnes of electrolyte). Financing is owner and bank money — a RMB 10 billion Bank of Communications facility (January 2024); two RMB 6 billion-class local government funds formed for the company in 2025–2026 no longer appear on its shareholder list, and a reported RMB 2 billion green bond cannot be found in any registry.
ecosystemRole: Cornex is a challenger in energy-storage cells — seventh globally on SNE Research's H1-2026 table at 30.2 GWh and 6.5%, roughly a quarter of CATL's 27.1% and 1.3 GWh behind CALB, and the twelfth and last name from that table to enter this corpus — reached by capacity-led expansion and below-cost bidding rather than by an incumbent's balance sheet. It also integrates its own cells into 20-foot containers (M5 5 MWh, M6 6.26 MWh) and C&I cabinets with CSA Group UL 9540A/1973/9540 and TÜV SÜD IEC 62619 certificates, but appears in no third-party integrator ranking, so its system business is a route to market for the cell. Its relevance to the AI-data-centre buyer is double-edged: a 2 GWh DC-side framework with TECO for data centres in Malaysia and Thailand on one side, and on the other a Chinese-owned cell that fails the prohibited-foreign-entity test, pays 25% Section 301 duty from 2026 and loses China's export rebate in 2027 — which is why its export map is Europe, the Middle East, Latin America and Southeast Asia rather than the United States.

productsAndServices.name: Energy-storage cells (储能电芯): 314Ah 聚能π, 472Ah, 588Ah and the 600Ah-plus family
productsAndServices.description: The core product and the basis of every ranking. The lineage the company states is 280Ah → 306/314Ah → 472Ah → 588Ah, with 625Ah, 648Ah, 684Ah and a 688Ah cell co-developed with CRRC Zhuzhou Institute shown or sampled since 2024. The 314Ah 聚能π (JuNeng Pi) cell went into the M5 container in mass production from February 2024; the 472Ah cell, defined with Huaneng's 华清储创, entered mass production on 30 June 2025 with 'up to 80 GWh' of capacity assigned; the 588Ah cell launched on 25 September 2025 with 'total planned capacity as high as 200 GWh' and mass delivery targeted for Q3 2026. A 100Ah cell serves residential and small storage. All are prismatic, liquid-cooled at pack level and sold with a 12,000-cycle rating.
highlights: PF288-588A (588Ah): 12,000 cycles, energy efficiency ≥94.5% at 0.5P on the spec page; 190 Wh/kg and 419 Wh/L (417 Wh/L in August 2026) and 96.5% efficiency in releases; 10.1 kg; 'directional pressure-relief channel' design
PF220-472A (472Ah): 1,510.4 Wh, 195 Wh/kg, 'up 50% on 314Ah'; optional cathode pre-lithiation for 15,000 cycles and 'five years of zero degradation'; mass production from 30 June 2025
PF173-314A (314Ah): 12,000 cycles, 185 Wh/kg; the 'long π' variant claims 15,000 cycles and a 25-year cycle life (18,000 cycles in a September 2024 release)

688Ah with CRRC Zhuzhou Institute (first cells 24 January 2025): '2.2 kWh, 10,000 cycles, calendar life over 20 years, 95% round-trip efficiency, near 200 Wh/kg, over 430 Wh/L', stacked electrodes and double-sided ceramic separator

Rank for H1 2026: SNE 7th (30.2 GWh, 6.5%), InfoLink, TrendForce and ICC 6th, Benchmark 5th (+116%), SPIR 3rd (523.6 GWh universe); FY2025 InfoLink and EVTank 9th, Benchmark 'top five'; 2024 outside InfoLink's and EVTank's top ten

The August 2023 pledge to sell 280Ah cells at no more than RMB 0.5/Wh ex-tax — 'about 40% below' the market — is the origin of the company's reputation for price-led entry; its 2025 tender bids ran at RMB 0.27–0.28/Wh
productsAndServices.positioning: Against CATL (27.1%), EVE (10.4%) and Hithium (10.0%) Cornex is a volume challenger whose share came from new capacity and price, and whose rank moves from third to seventh depending on which house counts; CALB and REPT sit 1.2–1.3 GWh above it on SNE's table and the three are separated by less than any house's methodology error. It is not named on the US Department of Defense 1260H list, unlike CATL, CALB, EVE and BYD, which is a distinction without a US market behind it. The 588Ah class puts it in the same format race as CATL's 587Ah, EVE's 628Ah and Hithium's 587Ah; the 688Ah programme with CRRC Zhuzhou runs in parallel with CRRC's 688Ah work with REPT and Great Power.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to Chinese utilities and integrators through tenders and framework agreements (CRRC Zhuzhou Institute, Dongfang Electric, CLOU, China Electrical Equipment Group, Huaneng, Goldwind) and to overseas integrators and developers through five European service centres and offices in the US, Brazil, Germany, the UK, Turkey, India, Singapore, Japan, Korea, South Africa and Australia.
targetSegments: Overseas storage developers and integrators (Europe, Middle East, Latin America, Southeast Asia)
productsAndServices.roadmap: 588Ah mass delivery from Q3 2026 with 200 GWh of planned capacity; 648Ah shown at CIBF and in Vietnam in 2026; Xiangyang scoped for '588Ah to 1,000Ah' cells; 'over 500 GWh' of planned capacity by end-2026 per the chairman.

productsAndServices.name: CORNEX M5 and M6 containers, CTP packs and the 浸默 (Jinmo) immersion safety system
productsAndServices.description: Factory-assembled 20-foot liquid-cooled DC blocks built on the company's own cells: the M5 (PF173-314A-C5015L, 5,015 kWh, 12 × 1P416S of 314Ah cells, 2,500 kW, 42.5 t) in mass production at Xiaogan since 1 February 2024, and the M6 (PF288-588A-C6262L, 6,262 kWh, 8 × 1P416S of 588Ah cells, 46 t), first shown on 472Ah cells at 6.28 MWh in 2025 and re-based on 588Ah cells from September 2025 with 'formal mass production this year' stated in June 2026. The CTP3.0 pack puts 104 588Ah cells in one 195.68 kWh box at 280 Wh/L without modules. 浸默 is a pack-level liquid-immersion fire-control system — a heat-runaway pack is flooded with a liquid extinguishing medium — first deployed at Three Gorges Energy's Qingyun phase 2 (201 MW / 402 MWh) in 2023; version 2.0 (2025) claims a six-second extinguish, 75% more cooling and 98% less stored liquid.
highlights: M5: UL 1973, UL 9540A and UL 9540 certificates from CSA Group (September 2024) and IEC 62619, IEC 63056 and EMC certificates from TÜV SÜD (October 2024); IP55 container, IP67 pack, −30 to 55 °C

M6: 'land-use efficiency up 33%, containers down 20%, service life up 20%', maximum operating temperature ≤35 °C, under 65 dB; 60 jobs per hour on the pack line against an industry 15, per the company
First 5 MWh system in Xinjiang (Karamay 48 MW / 96 MWh, 20 M5 units, 2024); first river-sea 'one-box' export shipment from Wuhan's Yangluo port (September 2025)

Named overseas M5 buyers: Bison Energy 1.5 GWh (US/AU/JP/IT, 2024), YN Energy 1.1 GWh (US, 2024), Immersa 1.25–2.5 GWh (UK, 2025), an unnamed Indian partner 5 GWh (2024), Intermepro (Costa Rica's first M5 Apex, 2026)
No third-party integrator ranking names Cornex; Benchmark's H1-2026 integrator top five is BYD, Sungrow, CATL, Tesla and HyperStrong
productsAndServices.positioning: A cell maker's system line, sold to give the cell a route to market where no integrator has yet designed it in — the same position CALB and Great Power occupy with their containers. It competes on the 20-foot 5–6 MWh format everyone now ships (CATL TENER, Hithium ∞Block, EVE Mr.Giant, Sungrow PowerTitan) and differentiates on the immersion safety system and price.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct and through EPC/design-institute agreements (Shanghai Electric Power Design Institute for M5 procurement and EPC, 2024); overseas through distributors and developers under framework agreements.
targetSegments: Overseas developers and integrators buying DC blocks
AI data-centre DC-side storage (TECO framework, Malaysia and Thailand)
productsAndServices.roadmap: M6 on 588Ah cells in mass production from 2026; a 2,000 V platform and 6.9–7.06 MWh variants shown in 2025; '百变金刚' modular 10-foot 3.13 MWh and 20-foot 6.26 MWh cabinets.

productsAndServices.name: Commercial and industrial storage cabinets
productsAndServices.description: Liquid-cooled outdoor cabinets on 280Ah and 314Ah cells: the OTS02-H233L (233 kWh, 110 kW, 1P260S of 280Ah) and OTS03-H261L (261 kWh, 130 kW, 1P260S of 314Ah), both 650–949 V DC, IP55, with pack-level and cabinet-level aerosol suppression, plus the 46.6 kWh PF173-280A-P46L liquid-cooled module. Sold in China through integrators and overseas through the household and C&I partners signed in 2026 (Growatt 5 GWh of 100Ah/314Ah cells, Sluxer, NKON).
highlights: OTS03-H261L: 261 kWh, 130 kW, 1035 × 1300 × 2305 mm, 2,650 kg, Modbus-RTU/TCP
Sits beside the residential and small-storage cell line (314Ah, 100Ah and 20Ah 'delivered at scale'; 120Ah, 50Ah and 30Ah 'about to enter mass production', June 2026)
Cornex 'entered the top five' in small storage on InfoLink's Q1 and H1 2026 tables
productsAndServices.positioning: A standard C&I cabinet in the 200–300 kWh class where Chinese competition is dense (Sungrow, HyperStrong, CATL's C&I lines); differentiation is the cell's price and the company's service network rather than a distinct architecture.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Integrators and distributors; overseas partners under framework agreements.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Not stated beyond the 2026 residential cell launches.

productsAndServices.name: EV traction, commercial-vehicle and marine batteries (珠峰 6C, CTP3.0 superfast, 320Ah marine)
productsAndServices.category: Traction batteries — passenger, commercial vehicle, marine
productsAndServices.description: The second business: prismatic LFP traction cells for passenger cars (PF210-145A 6C, PF300-173A 3C, PF300-166A, all 185 Wh/kg, with the 珠峰 'Everest' 6C cell launched 27 October 2025 at 190 Wh/kg and 420 Wh/L, '10 minutes of charging for 600 km' on an 800 V CTP3.0 pack), heavy-truck and bus cells (PF173-230A, PF173-324A, PF200-324A, PF200-268A; H02 and H03 truck packs), cylindrical light-mobility cells (45Ah full-tab, 20/30/50Ah) and a 320Ah marine cell with China Classification Society approval fitted to the 13,700-tonne 'Gezhouba' river vessel (24,000 kWh). Customers named by the company: Dongfeng (Fengshen E70, SKY EV01, L7; Dongfeng Liuzhou over 30 GWh over five years), FAW Bestune (over 170,000 vehicles cumulatively), SAIC Hongyan, SANY and Xiamen King Long trucks and buses, Zero One heavy trucks.
highlights: Cornex entered China's annual top fifteen for traction-battery installations for the first time in 2025 (13th in LFP), with 'over 300,000 vehicles and over 200 ships' fitted per Hubei Daily
珠峰 6C: double-sided ceramic separator, 'directional instant-venting sunroof', low-temperature electrolyte with ≥85% retention at −20 °C; range basis 'over 1,000 km'
Dongfeng Liuzhou nomination (August 2025): over 30 GWh of passenger and heavy-truck cells over five years

All three operating subsidiaries carry '道路机动车辆生产' (road motor vehicle production) as a licensed item in their business scope per a supplier's exchange filing (May 2025) — the first-party-adjacent trace of the owner's vehicle ambitions
productsAndServices.positioning: A distant follower in EV cells — outside SNE's global EV top ten and around 13th in China's LFP installations — whose traction line exists to fill capacity and to serve the owner's dealer network and, from 2027, the owner's own car brand.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: OEM nominations (定点) and direct supply to bus, truck and shipbuilders.
productsAndServices.roadmap: 楚能汽车 (Cornex Auto), a 50/50 venture of 恒信汽车集团 and 代德明 outside the listed-supplier chain, rolled out its first engineering prototype on 11 July 2026 and targets a mid-2027 launch of an extended-range SUV; the company's own site does not mention it.

productsAndServices.name: Sodium-ion cells
productsAndServices.description: Cylindrical sodium-ion cells for light mobility (10Ah, 16Ah, 26.5Ah; '91% capacity retained at −40 °C, over 10,000 cycles at 1C') launched in March 2026, and 165Ah and 350Ah prismatic sodium-ion cells for storage and marine use shown in Brazil and Wuhan in August–September 2026, including a 20-foot 1,956 kWh sodium-ion marine system. Materials come under the August 2025 agreement with BTR covering 'sodium core materials and next-generation solid-state materials'.
highlights: A '锂钠双系' (lithium and sodium dual-system) line for two-wheelers and ships
No shipment volume, customer or revenue disclosed; the product manual lists sodium-ion and solid-state as R&D routes
productsAndServices.positioning: Follows CATL, HiNa and Great Power into sodium-ion with a cold-climate and marine pitch; technical readiness without a disclosed market, the same state Great Power's line is in.

recentDevelopments.headline: Awarded the 10th Changjiang Quality Award (长江质量奖), Hubei's top quality prize, presented by the vice-governor
recentDevelopments.read: Provincial endorsement of a five-year-old company — the political capital behind the land, the funds and the bank line is visible in the awards as much as in the approvals.

recentDevelopments.headline: Xiangyang 70 GWh lithium-battery park starts production ten months after groundbreaking, 'two months ahead of plan'; 100Ah, 588Ah and 648Ah storage cells and fast-charge EV cells; about 400,000 cells a day at full run
recentDevelopments.read: The second 70–80 GWh plant commissioned in three weeks; speed of build is now the company's most verifiable competitive fact, and ramp is the thing to watch.

recentDevelopments.headline: Four Latin American agreements in São Paulo, including a 1.5 GWh cell framework with Windey (运达) for its Camaçari, Bahia plant and MoUs with Intermepro, ION Energy and JSN Energia
recentDevelopments.read: Brazil's local-content storage market reached through a Chinese wind-turbine maker's local plant — the export route that avoids the US entirely.

recentDevelopments.headline: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence: Cornex fifth in H1-2026 storage-cell shipments at 6.5% share, 'rose from the seventh to fifth' with 116% year-on-year growth
recentDevelopments.read: The second independent house to put the company inside the top five; the growth rate, not the rank, is the figure every house agrees on.

recentDevelopments.headline: Investigative piece '楚能的隐秘世界' (Tencent/赶碳号): no audited accounts ever published; two RMB 6 billion-class local government funds (宜昌楚宜新能, 武汉楚能股权投资基金) formed for the company and no longer on its shareholder list; a reported RMB 2 billion green bond untraceable in NAFMII or NDRC registries; RMB 66 billion of base capex against an estimated RMB 2.6–3.3 billion a year of Hengxin cash flow
recentDevelopments.read: The only public attempt to reconcile the capex with the money; the company did not respond, and the claims are unverified — but they are the questions a lender or a customer would ask.

recentDevelopments.headline: Yichang phase 2 (80 GWh, RMB 22 billion) commissioned ten months after groundbreaking; 'single-line efficiency up over 60%, over 800,000 cells a day at full production'; H1 2026 Yichang output over RMB 7.5 billion, shipments up 222%
recentDevelopments.read: The first hard output figure for any base — RMB 7.5 billion in a half from Yichang alone — and the only revenue-like number the company has let out.

recentDevelopments.headline: SNE Research H1-2026 global ESS cell table: Cornex seventh at 30.2 GWh and 6.5% share, its first appearance in the SNE top ten; market 461.3 GWh, +71%
recentDevelopments.read: The table this segment is typed against: a quarter of CATL's share, 1.3 GWh behind CALB and 1.2 behind REPT — a challenger by any reading, and a rank held by less than a rounding error.

recentDevelopments.headline: 经济观察报: the owner's separate 楚能汽车 (Cornex Auto, RMB 2 billion, 50/50 Hengxin Automobile Group and Dai Deming) rolled out its first engineering prototype on 11 July, targets a mid-2027 launch of an RMB 150,000–200,000 extended-range SUV, may take over the former WM Motor plant in Huanggang, and is 'self-funded at RMB 10 billion — no financing, no loans'
recentDevelopments.read: RMB 10 billion of the owner's money committed outside the battery company, in the most crowded segment of the Chinese car market, while the battery company's own capex depends on the same owner.

recentDevelopments.headline: 5 GWh European storage framework with KK Group, the new-energy subsidiary of Denmark's A.P. Moller Holding, covering design, supply, commissioning, O&M and recycling
recentDevelopments.read: A Maersk-family counterparty is the most bankable European name on the company's list; the agreement is a framework, not a purchase order.

recentDevelopments.headline: 2 GWh DC-side storage framework with TECO Electric & Machinery for AI data centres in Malaysia and Thailand over two years
recentDevelopments.read: The company's one named AI-data-centre exposure — Southeast Asian, DC-side and through a Taiwanese integrator, which is where a Chinese cell can still reach that buyer.

recentDevelopments.headline: Over 12 GWh of agreements at The smarter E Europe: IKAV/MoveOn/Cubenergy 3.4 GWh (Germany), Takom 2 GWh (Poland), InterConti 2 GWh (Ukraine), Orshar 1.6 GWh (Israel), Energy Investment 1 GWh (Romania), NKON 1 GWh, Sluxer up to 1 GWh residential
recentDevelopments.read: Europe is the export market of record; the counterparties are developers and distributors rather than utilities, and every figure is a framework ceiling.

recentDevelopments.headline: 12 GWh at SNEC: Dongfang Electric 8 GWh (314Ah and 588Ah framework), CHINT Electric 2 GWh and Alpha ESS 2 GWh of 588Ah cells; 588Ah 'total planned capacity as high as 200 GWh', pilot runs complete
recentDevelopments.read: The 588Ah class has a state-owned integrator's framework behind it before mass delivery — the order book leads the plant, as it did for the 472Ah.

recentDevelopments.headline: Tinci Materials (SZSE: 002709) raises its electrolyte supply commitment to Cornex's four bases from at least 550,000 t to at least 1,010,000 t through 2030
recentDevelopments.read: A listed supplier's disclosed volume is the closest thing to an audited demand forecast the company has; one million tonnes of electrolyte implies several hundred GWh of cells.

recentDevelopments.headline: 50 GWh of framework agreements at CIBF 2026: CRRC Zhuzhou Institute 25 GWh of large-capacity cells, CLOU 10 GWh, Wolong Storage 5 GWh, Cubenergy 5 GWh, Growatt 5 GWh (100Ah/314Ah residential)
recentDevelopments.read: CRRC Zhuzhou Institute's 25 GWh is the largest single signing in the company's history and pairs with the joint 688Ah cell — a covered integrator that now buys cells from Cornex, Great Power and REPT in parallel.

recentDevelopments.headline: InfoLink Q1-2026 table: Cornex sixth globally in storage-cell shipments (from ninth for 2025) and 'first into the top five' in small storage
recentDevelopments.read: The rank climbed three places in a quarter on capacity that was still being built; InfoLink's H1 note reads the trajectory as 'a good chance of the top five by year-end'.

recentDevelopments.headline: Hubei's 2026–2028 listing-reserve roster (金种子/银种子 — 472 and 664 companies) published by the provincial financial regulator carries no Cornex entity
recentDevelopments.read: The province's own IPO pipeline does not include its largest battery start-up — consistent with the chairman's 'no timetable' and the absence of any counselling filing.

recentDevelopments.headline: Cylindrical product line launched in Tianjin: 45Ah full-tab LFP for electric motorcycles (2.5C fast charge) and sodium-ion 10/16/26.5Ah cells with 91% capacity at −40 °C
recentDevelopments.read: The '锂钠双系' line widens the product count without a disclosed customer; sodium-ion remains an R&D route in the company's own manual.

recentDevelopments.headline: Two 100 GWh projects complete provincial filing (备案): Xiaogan phase 2 (2,348 mu, planned start May 2026) and Yichang phase 3 (1,468 mu, planned start February 2027), each adding drone, robot, semi-solid and solid-state lines
recentDevelopments.read: Another 200 GWh on paper on top of the 500 GWh plan; the filings, not a DRC approval, are the public record of the expansion.

recentDevelopments.headline: InfoLink FY2025 global storage-cell ranking: Cornex ninth, 'a new entrant to the global top ten', 2025 shipments 'over 90 GWh'; market 612.39 GWh, +94.59%
recentDevelopments.read: The full-year 2025 rank was ninth, not the 'top three' the company and its provincial patrons repeat — that phrase comes from SPIR's half-year table.

recentDevelopments.headline: Wuhan phase 2 signed with the municipal government: 80 GWh of EV and storage cells and packs, about RMB 22 billion, a 'Cornex Science Park' with three research institutes on a 'vehicles + energy' model, production from Q1 2027; the company states 'over 500 GWh of planned capacity'
recentDevelopments.read: The fourth RMB 22 billion-class base in eighteen months; the chairman's remark about 'intelligent connected vehicles' at the signing is the only first-party trace of the car plan.

recentDevelopments.headline: 5.5 GWh three-year storage framework in Dammam with Al Rajhi Electrical and Shanghai GreenGrid (亿电通) for Saudi local manufacturing; two weeks after a 6 GWh phased agreement with WeaCan and Kemet in Egypt witnessed by Egypt's electricity minister

policyExposure.exposure: The Section 301 duty on Chinese non-EV lithium-ion batteries rose from 7.5% to 25% on 1 January 2026, taking stacked duties on Chinese storage cells into the 50%-plus range. Cornex's only US-facing agreements are the 2024 frameworks with Bison Energy (1.5 GWh of M5 systems for US, Australian, Japanese and Italian markets) and YN Energy (1.1 GWh); no US signing appears among the 2026 agreements and the company has no US plant or licensing structure. Its export list — Europe, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Brazil, Malaysia and Thailand — reads as the map of markets the tariff does not reach.

As a Chinese-owned manufacturer Cornex is a prohibited foreign entity for the 45Y, 48E and 45X credits. Projects beginning construction from 2026 must keep prohibited-entity content below 45% of storage equipment cost (55% non-PFE, rising to 75% after 2029), and cells are roughly half of that cost, so a Cornex cell in a US credit-eligible project is close to unworkable. The company has published no mitigation and no US supply chain.

Cornex, Chuneng and Hengxin are not on the US Department of Defense's Section 1260H list of Chinese military companies as of 12 September 2026 — an OpenSanctions search returns no match — while CATL (January 2025) and BYD, CALB and EVE (65 additions of 8 June 2026) are. The distinction bars nothing today, since Cornex has no US federal customers, but it separates it from four of the six companies above it on SNE's table.

The Ministry of Finance and State Taxation Administration announcement of 9 January 2026 cut the export VAT rebate on batteries from 9% to 6% for 1 April to 31 December 2026 and to zero from 1 January 2027, after the 13% to 9% cut of December 2024. The company's overseas share is its fastest-growing line and every 2026 framework is priced against a rebate that disappears in 2027; InfoLink attributes part of the industry's 2026 export surge to a pull-forward ahead of the cliff.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess that Cornex is a challenger and not an incumbent in energy-storage cells, and that its rank is a property of the counting house rather than of the company. Basis: SNE places it seventh for H1 2026 at 30.2 GWh and 6.5% — a quarter of CATL's share, 1.3 GWh behind CALB and 1.2 behind REPT; InfoLink, TrendForce and ICC place it sixth, Benchmark fifth, SPIR third; for FY2025 InfoLink and EVTank say ninth, Benchmark 'top five'. The 'global top three' the company and its provincial patrons repeat is SPIR's half-year and a monthly table. On every table it is the fastest riser (Benchmark +116%), which is the challenger definition, and on none does it carry leader language.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess that the company's financing model — one car dealer's cash flow, provincial land and a bank line funding RMB 60 billion-plus of plants — is the central risk, and that it is unexamined because nothing is audited. Basis: no financial statement, shareholder table or registered-capital figure has ever been published by the company; the RMB 10 billion Bank of Communications facility is its only announced financing; two RMB 6 billion-class local government funds formed for it in 2025–2026 no longer appear on its shareholder list; a reported RMB 2 billion green bond cannot be found in any registry; and the parent group's revenue fell in 2025 while its owner pledged RMB 10 billion to a car venture outside the battery company.

3. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that speed of build is the company's real product and that its share has been bought with capacity and price rather than technology. Basis: two 70–80 GWh plants commissioned ten months after groundbreaking in August 2026; a 588Ah cell that follows CATL's and EVE's formats by about a year; tender bids of RMB 0.27–0.28/Wh in 2025 at or below industry cash cost; and a supplier commitment (1.3 million tonnes of cathode) sized for several hundred GWh. The claim of break-even from July 2025 is a chairman's sentence with no figure behind it and cuts against the pricing record.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that there is no IPO in preparation and that the absence is structural rather than pending. Basis: no application at HKEX, no CSRC overseas-listing filing, no counselling registration with the Hubei CSRC bureau, no entry on Hubei's own 2026–2028 listing-reserve roster of 1,136 companies, and a chairman on record that there is 'no clear timetable'. The company is already a joint-stock company, so the missing step is the counselling filing, not a reorganisation; the two government funds' departure is consistent with a pre-IPO round that did not proceed.

5. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the export book is real in direction and soft in quantity, and that it points away from the United States by design. Basis: roughly 40 GWh of 2026 overseas agreements across Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Germany, Poland, Ukraine, Romania, Israel, Denmark, Brazil, Argentina, Malaysia and Thailand — every one a framework or MoU — against no 2026 US signing; a Chinese-owned cell fails the prohibited-foreign-entity ratio, pays 25% Section 301 duty from 2026 and loses China's export rebate in 2027. The one AI-data-centre link, TECO's 2 GWh for Malaysia and Thailand, is DC-side and Southeast Asian for the same reasons.

6. **(Low confidence)** We assess that the owner's car venture will divert capital and attention from the cell business rather than feed it. Basis: 楚能汽车 sits outside Cornex (50/50 Hengxin and Dai), is 'self-funded at RMB 10 billion — no financing, no loans', targets a mid-2027 launch into the most crowded segment of the Chinese market, and all three Cornex operating subsidiaries already hold vehicle-production licences in their business scope; the Wuhan subsidiary was incorporated in 2017 under the president's name, which suggests the corporate history is longer and more vehicle-shaped than the 2021 founding story. The company's own channels do not mention the venture, so the assessment rests on trade press and a supplier's filing.

**Collection gaps.** No audited accounts, revenue, profit, debt, headcount or shareholder table exists from the company or any regulator; every ownership percentage is aggregator data and the three versions in circulation do not agree. The 'Hubei DRC approval of 20 May 2026 for three projects adding 290 GWh' carried in the prior plan row could not be found — fgw.hubei.gov.cn returned HTTP 412 on six probes, yichang.gov.cn was policy-denied, and no combination of the known phases sums to 290 GWh; the public record of the expansion is the February–March 2026 filings for two 100 GWh projects. No CATL litigation against Cornex exists in the public record. The exact Xiangyang commissioning day is 'end of August' in the company's release and 30 August in the plan row. SNE's own release page for the H1-2026 storage table was not located; the CnEVPost, Sina and Sohu copies agree. Prior-career biographies of the president and executive vice president are unpublished. The CSRC Hubei bureau's monthly counselling spreadsheets returned an anti-bot page and were read from the channel text only.

**Indicators to watch.** *Any listing-application proof at HKEXnews, a CSRC overseas-listing filing, or a 辅导备案 with the Hubei CSRC bureau:* would reverse Judgment 4 and convert the calendar row from quarterly to dated. *SNE's FY2026 and H1-2027 storage tables:* a rank inside the top five on SNE — not SPIR — would move the role question toward incumbent; a fall below REPT and CALB would confirm the rank is contested. *Ramp at Xiangyang and Yichang phase 2 and the Wuhan phase 2 start (Q1 2027):* a published post-August effective-capacity figure above 110 GWh is the first test of the 500 GWh plan. *An audited statement, a bond prospectus or a bank syndication document:* the first financial disclosure of any kind would resolve Judgment 2 one way or the other. *A 1260H addition or a US enforcement action naming Cornex:* would close the one US distinction it holds. *China's export-rebate cliff on 1 January 2027 and Section 301 stacking:* watch overseas signings and prices in Q4 2026 for pull-forward. *楚能汽车's mid-2027 launch and any Cornex-side vehicle production:* would confirm Judgment 6's diversion.
